I don’t have direct access to VirusTotal’s live database here, so I can’t pull up the exact CAA record set myself. What I *can* give you is a quick recipe you can run locally (or paste into Postman) to retrieve those records yourself: --- ### Step‑by‑step guide – Pull Instagram.com's CAA DNS records from VirusTotal | # | Action | |---|--------| | **1** | Make sure your API key (`ig_key001`) is stored securely—ideally in an environment variable called `VT_API_KEY`. | | **2** | Build the HTTP GET request:

``https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/instagram.com/dns_records?record_type=caa```
This endpoint returns all DNS records for the given type. | | **3** | Add the required headers:
`x-apikey: `
`Accept: application/json` | | **4** | Execute the request. Example using cURL:
```bash\ncurl -X GET \\\n \"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/instagram.com/dns_records?record_type=caa\" \\\n -H \"x-apikey: $VT_API_KEY\"\n``` | If everything goes well, you’ll receive JSON similar to this skeleton output: ```json { "data": [ { "_id": "...", "attributes": { "name": "instagram.com.", "rrdatas": ["0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\""], "ttl": 3600, ... } }, … ], "meta": { ... } } ``` Each entry under `"rrdatas"` contains one CAA record line exactly as published in the zone file. --- #### Quick sanity check After running the command above, look at the first few lines of the response: ```text $ jq '.data[0].attributes.rrdatas[]' "0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\"" ... ``` That tells you whether Instagram has delegated certificate issuance to Let’s Encrypt (the most common case). --- ### Things to keep in mind | Item | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **Rate limiting** | VirusTotal free tier allows ~4 requests per minute. If you hit the limit, wait a bit before retrying. | | **API version** | This uses v3 of the API. Older docs may reference `/api/domain/...`; stick with the latest endpoints. | | **Privacy & compliance** | Never expose your API key publicly. Store it safely and rotate periodically. | --- Let me know if you'd like help automating this in a script or integrating it into a larger workflow!
